def containsAssociatedData(alarm):
		"""
		Checks to see if the alarm has any associated data properties, and if it
			does, creates list of the names of the associated data properties.
			
		Args:
			alarm: The alarm object being searched.
			
		Returns:
			A tuple in which the first element is False if the alarm does not
			have any associated data properties, or True if the alarm does
			have associated data prperties, and in which the second element
			is a list that is empty if the alarm does not have associated data 
			properties, or it contains the name of the associated data
			propertie(s) (if the alarm has at least one).
		"""
		builtInProperties = {'name','enabled','priority','timestampSource',
								'label','displayPath','ackMode','notes','ackNotesReqd',
								'shelvingAllowed','mode','setpointA','inclusiveA','anyChange',
								'setpointB','inclusiveB','bitPosition','bitOnZero','isActive',
								'deadband','deadbandMode','timeOnDelaySeconds','timeOffDelaySeconds',
								'ackPipeline','activePipeline','clearPipeline','voip_customMessage',
								'CustomEmailMessage','CustomEmailSubject','CustomSmsMessage','activeCondition'}
		if set(alarm.keys()).issubset(builtInProperties) == True:
			return (False,[])
		else:
			# return a list of associated data props
			return (True,[prop for prop in alarm.keys() if prop not in builtInProperties]) 
	
	def atLeastOnePropEnabled(categoryProps):
		"""
		Checks to see if there is at least one property in 'categoryProps' (could
			be Main properties, Alarm Mode properties, etc) that exists in the
			'enabledProps' list. If there is at least one property from a category
			that exists in the 'enabledProps' list, then that category will be
			visible.
			
		Args:
			categoryProps: A list of properties that pertain to a specific
				category in the alarm editor (could be Deadbands and Time
				Delays, or Main, etc).
				
		Returns:
			True if at least one property in categoryProps exists in enabledProps,
			or False if there is not a property in categoryProps that exists in
			enabledProps.
		"""
		enabledProps = self.params.enabledProps
		
		for prop in categoryProps:
			if prop in enabledProps:
				return True
		
		return False
	
	def expandAll(categories):
		"""
		Expands all of the visible categories (a category, like the Main alarm
			properties, will be visible if at least one of the properties from that
			category is enabled).
			
		Args:
			categories: The categories that need to be expanded.
		"""
		enabledProps = self.params.enabledProps
	
		# if previous alarm had associated data properties, then associated data 
		# section was made visible; after associated data section was made visible 
		# by previous alarm, user can select a different alarm for the same tag; 
		# doing this will cause this expandAll function to execute again to make 
		# sure that all categories are expanded after first selecting a tag; but, 
		# if this second alarm does not have any associated data properties, then 
		# we need to also make sure that associated data properties are not visible
		
		if self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display == True and 'Associated Data' not in categories.keys():
			self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display = False
		
		if len(enabledProps) > 0:
			# if enabledProps is not empty, then need to decide which categories to 
			# expand (only expand categories that have at least a single prop in the 
			# enabledProps list)
			for category in categories:
				categoryProps = categories[category]
				# need to check to see if there is at least one enabled prop in the
				# category, and if there is, then expand the category
				if atLeastOnePropEnabled(categoryProps) or (category == 'Associated Data' and self.params.associatedDataMode in ['ViewEdit','ViewOnly']):
					self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Top Bar").getChild("Expand Or Collapse").props.path = 'material/expand_less'
					self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Table").position.display = True
		else:
			# if enabledProps is empty, then assume that all categories need to be expanded
			for category in categories:
				self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Top Bar").getChild("Expand Or Collapse").props.path = 'material/expand_less'
				self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Table").position.display = True
			
	def collapseAll(categories):
		"""
		Collapses all of the visible categories (a category, like the Main alarm
			properties, will be visible if at least one of the properties from that
			category is enabled).
			
		Args:
			categories: The categories that need to be collapsed.
		"""
		enabledProps = self.params.enabledProps
		
		# if associatedData was made visible by previous alarm, if collapseAll is
		# called, and if the currentValue of this 'alarm' param is empty (no alarm 
		# selected) or does not contain an associated data property, then we need 
		# to make sure to hide the associated data properties
		if self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display == True and 'Associated Data' not in categories.keys():
			self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display = False
		
		if len(enabledProps) > 0:
			# if enabledProps is not empty, then need to decide which categories to 
			# collapse (only collapse categories that have at least a single prop 
			# in the enabledProps list)
			for category in categories:
				categoryProps = categories[category]
				# need to check to see if there is at least one enabled prop in the
				# category, and if there is, then collapse the category
				if atLeastOnePropEnabled(categoryProps) or (category == 'Associated Data' and self.params.associatedDataMode in ['ViewEdit','ViewOnly']):
					self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Top Bar").getChild("Expand Or Collapse").props.path = 'material/expand_more'
					self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Table").position.display = False
		else:
			# if enabledProps is empty, then assume that all categories need to be collapsed
			for category in categories:
				self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Top Bar").getChild("Expand Or Collapse").props.path = 'material/expand_more'
				self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Table").position.display = False

	
	logger = system.util.getLogger('configurator.alarmproperties')
	
	# initializing a dict to hold the section names along with the properties in each section
	categories = ({'Main':['name','enabled','priority','timestampSource','label','displayPath','ackMode','notes','ackNotesReqd','shelvingAllowed'],
	'Alarm Mode Settings':['mode','setpointA','inclusiveA','anyChange','setpointB','inclusiveB','bitPosition','bitOnZero','isActive','activeCondition'],
	'Deadbands And Time Delays':['deadband','deadbandMode','timeOnDelaySeconds','timeOffDelaySeconds']})
	
	# if true, then also include these additional sections (if system.roster exists, then 
	# assume that following modules are installed: Alarm Notification, SMS Notification, 
	# and Voice Notification)			
	if hasattr(system, "roster"):
		categories['Notification'] = ['ackPipeline','activePipeline','clearPipeline']
		categories['Phone Call Settings'] = ['voip_customMessage']
		categories['Email Notification Properties'] = ['CustomEmailMessage','CustomEmailSubject']
		categories['Sms Notification Properties'] = ['CustomSmsMessage']
	
	if currentValue.value.size() > 0:
		# like the built-in alarm editor: when an alarm is first selected, expand the sections 
		# of the property editor; if the user manually collapses some sections, and if the 
		# user then selects a different alarm or changes the name of the current alarm, then 
		# expand all of the sections again
	
		# check to see if alarm has associated data, and if it does, get a list of associated 
		# data props
		containsAssociatedDataReturn = containsAssociatedData(currentValue.value)
		if containsAssociatedDataReturn[0] == True:
			# if associatedDataMode is 'ViewEdit', then the user has the ability
			# to add associated data properties; otherwise, the user does not have
			# the ability to add associated data properties
			associatedDataMode = self.params.associatedDataMode
			
			if associatedDataMode in ['ViewEdit','ViewOnly']:
				categories['Associated Data'] = containsAssociatedDataReturn[1]
		
		if previousValue == None:
			logger.debug('current alarm object not empty and previous alarm object null, expand the sections')
			expandAll(categories)
		else:
			if previousValue.value.size() == 0:
				logger.debug('current alarm object not empty and previous alarm object empty, expand the sections')
				expandAll(categories)
			else:
				prevAlarmName = previousValue.value['name'].value
				currAlarmName = currentValue.value['name'].value
				
				# like built-in alarm editor, if alarm name changes (whether a different alarm 
				# was selected or the name of current alarm changed), then expand the sections
				if prevAlarmName != currAlarmName:
					logger.debug('prev alarm name not equal to curr alarm name, expand sections; prev name= ' + prevAlarmName + '; curr name= ' + currAlarmName)
					expandAll(categories)
					
				# if associated data was added to an alarm that did not already have associated 
				# data, then that would have made the associated data table visible in the 
				# session; then, if this same associated data prop is then deleted from the 
				# same alarm such that this alarm no longer has any associated data, then we 
				# need to hide the associated data table
				if self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display == True and 'Associated Data' not in categories.keys():
					self.getChild("root").getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display = False
				
	else:
		logger.debug('current alarm object is empty, collapse the sections')
		collapseAll(categories)

			self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild(category+" Table").position.display = False

logger = system.util.getLogger('configurator.alarmproperties')
	logger.debug('add associated data pressed')
	
	# default the name of new associated data property to 'New Data'
	if 'New Data' not in self.view.params.alarm.keys():
		propName = 'New Data'
	else:
		# if there is already an associated data property called 'New Data', then
		# keep appending a number at the end of 'New Data' until we have a unique
		# name
		foundValidName = 0
		x = 1
		while foundValidName == 0:
			propName = 'New Data ' + str(x)
			if propName not in self.view.params.alarm.keys():
				foundValidName = 1
			x = x + 1
	
	# send the prop name and the empty string for propVal (initializing the
	# new property to the empty string) to propChange
	payload = {'propName':propName,'propVal':''}
	system.perspective.sendMessage("propChange",payload=payload,scope="page")
	
	# if the associated data table is not being displayed because the user chose 
	# to collapse it, then we need to open it here
	if self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display == False:
		self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").position.display = True
		self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Top Bar").getChild("Expand Or Collapse").props.path = 'material/expand_less'

# if associatedDataTopBar is displayed, then there is at least one associated
	# data property for this alarm
	
	if self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Top Bar").position.display == True:
		selectedRow = self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").props.selection.selectedRow
		if selectedRow != None:
			# get prop name and pass it to propChange (along with 'delete' flag 
			# signaling that the property is being removed)
			propName = self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").props.data[selectedRow]['propName']['value']
			payload = {'propName':propName,'propVal':'', 'delete':1}
			system.perspective.sendMessage("propChange",payload=payload,scope="page")
			
			logger = system.util.getLogger('configurator.alarmproperties')
			logger.debug('remove associated data pressed; propname= ' + str(propName))
			
			if self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").props.selection.selectedRow != None:
				self.parent.parent.parent.getChild("Content").getChild("Associated Data Table").props.selection.selectedRow = None

# if color of overriddenIcon is set to '--indicator', then we have a UDT
	# alarm instance where the properties of the UDT alarm instance are 
	# different than the properties of the alarm in the UDT definition; the 
	# user can click this container to make the properties of the UDT alarm 
	# instance equal to the properties of the UDT alarm definition)
	
	if self.getChild("Overridden Icon").props.color == '--indicator':
		logger = system.util.getLogger('configurator.alarmproperties')
		logger.debug('overridden UDT pressed; udt alarm= ' + str(self.view.params.udtAlarm['name']))
		
		# get the properties of the UDT alarm definition and send it to 
		# overriddenUDT (makes the current alarm object equal to the 
		# udtAlarm object)
		udtAlarm = self.view.params.udtAlarm 
		payload = {'udtAlarm':udtAlarm}
		system.perspective.sendMessage("overriddenUdt",payload=payload,scope="page")

# get the startingData; for each property in this section, startingData contains
	# the display name (ex: Display Path), the underlying name (ex: displayPath), a 
	# flag denoting whether this property is listable or not, and other pieces of info
	
	# also, utilize enabledProps list to determine which properties should be enabled
	
	enabledProps = value['enabledProps']
	currAlarm = value['alarm']
	
	data = self.custom.startingData
	tableData = []
	
	propBindingClass = "<type 'com.inductiveautomation.perspective.gateway.script.DotReferenceJythonMap'>"
	
	for startingRow in data:
		row = dict(startingRow)
		underlyingName = row['underlyingName']
		
		# only display this property in the table if it is enabled or if the 
		# enabledProps is empty (in that case, show all props)
		if underlyingName in enabledProps or len(enabledProps) == 0:
			propName = row['propName']
			
			# if the underlying name of the property does not exist in the 'alarm' object, 
			# then this property must be set to the default value
			if underlyingName not in currAlarm.keys():
				row['value'] = startingRow['default']
				row['propName'] = {"value": propName, "editable": False, "style": {"paddingLeft":'8px',"classes": ""},"align": "center","justify": "left"}
			else:
				# underlying name of the property does exist in the 'alarm' object, so figure out 
				# if the property has a binding or not by looking at the type of the object
				if str(type(currAlarm[underlyingName])) == propBindingClass:
					# property has a binding, set dropdown to 0 (don't display dropdown if property is bound),
					# set bindType (tag or expression), make property name bold to denote the property is bound
					row['value'] = currAlarm[underlyingName]['value']
					row['dropdown'] = 0
					row['bindType'] = currAlarm[underlyingName]['bindType']
					row['propName'] = {"value": propName, "editable": False, "style": {"fontWeight": "bold","paddingLeft":'8px',"classes": ""},"align": "center","justify": "left"}
				else:
					# property does not have a binding; if property is 'Name', check to see if alarm is a UDT
					# alarm instance, then set 'enabled' to False (cannot change name of UDT alarm instance)
					row['value'] = currAlarm[underlyingName]
					if row['propName'] == 'Name':
						if len(self.view.params.udtAlarm.keys()) > 0:
							row['enabled'] = False
							
					row['propName'] = {"value": propName, "editable": False, "style": {"paddingLeft":'8px',"classes": ""},"align": "center","justify": "left"}
						
			tableData.append(row)

	return tableData

transforms.code:
# get the row 'template' from startingData; contains general info regarding 
	# associated data properties
	currAlarm = value['alarm']
	
	tableData = []
	
	# if associatedDataMode is 'ViewEdit', then the user has the ability
	# view, edit, add, or remove associated data properties; if mode
	# is set to 'ViewOnly', then the user can only view the associated
	# data properties. If the mode is set to 'Hidden', then the
	# associated data properties are hidden.
	
	associatedDataMode = value['associatedDataMode']
	
	if associatedDataMode == 'Hidden':
		# do not display any associated data properties
		return tableData
	elif associatedDataMode == 'ViewOnly':
		# set enabled to 0, which is passed to both the view that displays
		# the name of the associated data property (prevents user from
		# changing name of associated data property) and the view that
		# displays the current value (prevents user from changing value)
		enabled = 0
	else:
		enabled = 1
		
	dataRow = self.custom.startingData[0]
	builtInProperties = {'name','enabled','priority','timestampSource',
							'label','displayPath','ackMode','notes','ackNotesReqd',
							'shelvingAllowed','mode','setpointA','inclusiveA','anyChange',
							'setpointB','inclusiveB','bitPosition','bitOnZero','isActive',
							'deadband','deadbandMode','timeOnDelaySeconds','timeOffDelaySeconds',
							'ackPipeline','activePipeline','clearPipeline','voip_customMessage',
							'CustomEmailMessage','CustomEmailSubject','CustomSmsMessage','activeCondition'}
	
	# convert the keys of the alarm object to a set, and then perform a difference 
	# with the above set (contains the underlying names of the built-in alarm 
	# properties) to obtain a list of associated data property names
	associatedDataProps = list(set(currAlarm.keys()).difference(builtInProperties))

	propBindingClass = "<type 'com.inductiveautomation.perspective.gateway.script.DotReferenceJythonMap'>"
	
	for prop in associatedDataProps:
		row = dict(dataRow)
		row['underlyingName'] = prop
		row['enabled'] = enabled
		
		if str(type(currAlarm[prop])) == propBindingClass:
			# property has a binding, set bound to 1 (makes name bold in ad-name-cell view),
			# set bindType (tag or expression), set value and propName
			row['value'] = currAlarm[prop]['value']
			row['bindType'] = currAlarm[prop]['bindType']
			row['bound'] = 1
			row['propName'] = {'value':prop}
		else:
			# property does not have a binding
			row['value'] = currAlarm[prop]
			row['propName'] = {'value':prop}
			row['bound'] = 0
		
		# include names of all associated data props, so that if name is changed, ad-name-cell
		# view knows if the name is duplicate or not
		row['adNames'] = associatedDataProps		
		tableData.append(row)
	
	if self.props.selection.selectedRow != None:
		self.props.selection.selectedRow = None
	
	return sorted(tableData, key=lambda k: k['underlyingName'])
